newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Union Miniere buys U.S. firm SBS.
newsitem.headline: Union Miniere buys U.S. firm SBS.

text.p: Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere said in a statement it bought all the shares of U.S. firm South Boston Semiconductors (SBS).
It gave no financial details of the deal.

SBS, located in Boston, employs 30 people and expects to make a 1996 turnover of 2.5 million dollars, Union Miniere said in a statement. The company is specialised in the transformation of semiconductor materials into polished wafers for electronic applications.
Specific markets are silicon wafers for sensors, germanium substrates for space solar cells and silicon reclaim for the electronic industry.
Union Miniere said SBS would be integrated into UM Germanium & Special Metals, one of the business units of the Union Miniere Group.

"The acquisition of SBS increases the capacity of UM to respond to the growth in demand for germanium substrates for solar cells. In addition, it introduces UM in some promising semiconductor niches," the UM statement said.
"It is part of the strategy of the UM Group to extend its international presence in high-technology areas," it added.
